We're just 11 days from the midterm elections, and Donald Trump and his allies
are ramping up efforts to steal them.

This week, we learned the Trump administration asked a federal agency to hack
voting machines, the president lost it - again - on reporters, and [Trump
censor-in-chief Brendan Carr](https://zeteo.com/p/meet-trumps-censor-in-chief)
warned broadcasters against "fake polls" (we all know what that means).

Needless to say, Trump and his allies were extremely busy harming American
democracy, undermining the Constitution, and hurting societies worldwide.
Here's more from 'This Week in Democracy - Week 92':

#### **Saturday, Oct. 17 - Meta Suspends No Kings Instagram Account, Blames
'Error'**

Meta [temporarily suspended](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2026/oct/18/no-kings-instagram-account-suspended-during-protests) the No
Kings Instagram account for several hours while thousands of rallies were
[held](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/16/no-kings-early-voting-
midterm-elections) in all 50 states and in Washington, D.C., to encourage
people to vote early in the looming midterm elections.

The company later apologized, claiming the suspension was a result of an
"automated action … clearly taken in error."

#### **Sunday, Oct. 18 - Trump Cut Legal Immigration in Half Early This Year**

The _New York Times_
[reported](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/10/18/us/trump-immigrant-
visas-decline.html) that legal immigration was cut in half early this year
after the Trump administration implemented policies to block visas for
immigrants from nearly half of the world.

The State Department issued just 26,000 immigrant visas in February, down from
an average of 52,000 per month in the years before Trump's second term. And
while federal judges have ordered the Trump administration to resume visa
issuances, the vast majority of blocked applicants are still awaiting their
approval.

#### **Monday, Oct. 19 - The Trump Admin Asked CISA to Hack Voting Machine**

ProPublica [published](https://www.propublica.org/article/cisa-election-
security-donald-trump) a bombshell report detailing a request during the early
months of the Trump administration for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure
Security Agency, which is meant to protect election systems, to secretly
acquire a voting machine, hack it, and give the findings not to the voting
machine company - but to the White House.

The shocking request, which made employees fear they were engaging in
political interference, was rejected in part because Elon Musk's so-called
Department of Government Efficiency laid off the same agents who would have
completed the operation, ProPublica reported.

#### **Tuesday, Oct. 20 - Trump Loses It at Reporters, Wants Them Removed From
White House**

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump
[snapped](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2112619453091344853?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2112619453091344853%7Ctwgr%5Eaf6939d0f6af861365bb534fb7424cd7de3a24a0%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewrepublic.com%2Fpost%2F216863%2Fyou-
better-be-careful-trump-lashes-white-house-reporters) at _The_ _Independent_
's Andrew Feinberg multiple times, pointing a finger at him and saying, "I
don't know who the hell you are, but you better be careful," and later [asking
him](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2112623065263726702) if he was a "sick
person." He also [shushed and
yelled](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2112617623670104333?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2112617623670104333%7Ctwgr%5Eaf6939d0f6af861365bb534fb7424cd7de3a24a0%7Ctwcon%5Es1_&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fnewrepublic.com%2Fpost%2F216863%2Fyou-
better-be-careful-trump-lashes-white-house-reporters) at a female reporter to
"wait" before going on to take a male reporter's question instead.

Meanwhile, the _New York Times_
[reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/20/us/politics/trump-white-house-
media.html) that, in August, Trump floated the idea of replacing the White
House briefing room with a swimming pool, which would effectively remove news
organizations from the White House.

#### **Wednesday, Oct. 21 - Trump's FCC Chair Warns Against Airing 'Fake'
Polls**

On Twitter, FCC chair Brendan Carr
[warned](https://x.com/BrendanCarrFCC/status/2112913475705934326) broadcasters
against airing so-called "Fake Polls," writing that they should avoid engaging
in what he called "News Distortions or running Broadcast Hoaxes by airing
Polls that would violate their regulatory behavior." The warning comes after
Trump has
[repeatedly](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117184527741564500)
[criticized](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117151357800143501)
polls showing low support for him and his policies.

Later, the sole Democratic FCC commissioner, Anna Gomez, [pushed
back](https://x.com/AGomezFCC/status/2112934159609946512) against Carr,
tweeting that "broadcasters who report publicly available polling data should
never be punished when a poll is wrong," and adding that "FCC rules on news
distortions or hoaxes do not apply to a station that reports this data in good
faith."

#### **Thursday, Oct. 22 - Trump Files Lawsuit to Block Possible Dem Win in
Alaska**

The Trump administration
[filed](https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/28830814-us-v-alaska/) a
preemptive lawsuit to block the certification of Alaska's U.S. Senate election
if Democratic candidate Mary Peltola wins - a move that could affect a race
that may very well decide which party controls the Senate during the second
half of Trump's presidency.

An election law professor [told](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/23/politics/doj-
sues-alaska-dan-sullivan-us-senate) CNN the lawsuit is centered around a
"strange and unusual" legal theory, and raised questions about how the courts
could practically intervene in the way the DOJ is proposing.

#### **Friday, Oct. 23 - Trump Expected to Nix Tariffs to Help Republican
Senator in Midterms**

The _Wall Street Journal_
[reported](https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/trump-expected-to-remove-some-
tariffs-on-canada-in-bid-to-help-susan-collins-6a89ed1d?st=Nmrg4V) that the
Trump administration is getting rid of its 50% tariffs on some Canadian
agricultural and forestry products in an effort to help tip the scales for
Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race for re-election in Maine against
Democratic candidate Troy Jackson.

"The action is intended to help Collins, who has requested relief from tariffs
that hit Maine industries and consumers," the _Journal_ wrote.
